title: Lesson 3: The Agent Loop: Perceive, Reason, Act, Observe, and Where Your Code Lives
description: The one while loop that turns a language model into an agent: the five stages of the loop, the pseudocode that runs underneath every framework, and exactly which parts of it are your code versus the runtime's.

questions.question: The while loop that repeatedly calls the model and executes tools is best understood as whose responsibility?
options: Runtime or framework code, not something you write
A portion you must hand-code yourself for every agent you build
A detail that varies by which model you choose
The same thing as the system prompt you author
questions.explanation: The loop itself is runtime code; your work lives in what the loop touches, such as tools and schemas, state, stopping criteria, logging, and memory.

questions.question: Which set of concerns is the code you actually own in an agent?
options: The loop's iteration order and model selection
Tool schemas, state, stopping criteria, logging, and memory
The provider's network stack, tokenization layer, and rate limits
The model weights and inference hardware
questions.explanation: The runtime supplies the loop, but the tool schemas, state handling, stopping criteria, telemetry, and memory layer are yours to design and maintain.

questions.question: Why is a hard stopping condition essential in a production agent loop?
options: It keeps the model from changing or overwriting its own instructions
It guarantees every step produces a correct result
It removes the need to validate tool output
It prevents the loop from running indefinitely and burning budget
questions.explanation: A loop with no exit can keep retrying and spending tokens without converging, so a max-iteration or budget limit bounds the run.
